00408490.note: Identified 2026-09-23 from disassembly, not decompilation. CGxDevice::RsPop (00685fb0) shrinks three growable arrays through the same idiom -- round the new count up to the array's grow quantum, then Reserve -- so the three helpers it calls are one Reserve per element type, told apart by the index scaling in each: `leal (,%eax,4)` here, so 4-byte elements -- the render-state MARK STACK at CGxDevice+0x14, which frozen calls m_stackOffsets. **This address was previously linked to CGxDevice::RsPush, and that was wrong.** The body is SMemReAlloc(data, count*4, ...), store to +8, copy min(count, old) elements: a growable-array Reserve, with nothing render-state about it. It has only four callers in the whole binary, two of which use it on CGxDevice+0x14. The bad link held RsPop's call-order recall at 0% and made RsPop look as if it called RsPush. Diverged because frozen is 64-bit: its m_stackOffsets is TSGrowableArray<size_t>, 8 bytes per element against the reference's 4. The reference's real RsPush is still unidentified and may well be inlined -- it is two lines, and no small function near RsPop matches it. The name it used to carry, for reference: TSGrowableArray<unsigned __int64>::Reserve. EXCLUDED 2026-09-27, and the status change matters more than it looks. It was `diverged` naming TSGrowableArray<unsigned __int64>::Reserve -- a correct identification, but that name is a header-only template instantiation and binds to nothing, and `diverged` does NOT veto the automatic matchers the way `unlinked` does. The false link then rendered INTO the decompilation of RsPop, which is how it was noticed -- GxRsPop appeared to call RsPush. 006a43d0.note: CGxDeviceD3d::IStateSyncLights. PORTED 2026-09-23, replacing the entry that said this was deliberately left a stub because CGxDevice had no light state. 006a99e0.note: CGxDeviceD3d::IXformSetViewport, found by running --diff on IStateSync: every other callee matched in order and this showed as the one unlinked `- 006a99e0`. Identified from four agreeing facts: it calls DeviceCurWindow (00682d70); it reads six consecutive floats at +0xf70..+0xf84, which is m_viewport as {x.l, x.h, y.l, y.h, z.l, z.h}, and forms x.l * maxX + 0.5 and (1.0 - y.h) * maxY + 0.5 as its first two terms; it calls vtable 0xbc and 0xbc / 4 = 47 = SetViewport; and it ends by storing 0 to +0xf6c, which is intF6C, the flag IStateSync tests before calling it. STATUS faithful BY HAND, because the branch-shape check misjudges this one. The reference has four branches and frozen has one, but two of the four are not control flow at all: they reload X and Y as signed 32-bit and add 4294967296.0 (2^32, the constant at 0x009e23ac) when negative, which is only the x87 idiom for converting a DWORD to floating point. X and Y are DWORDs in frozen, so the C++ conversions do that implicitly and reproducing the branches would be copying codegen. The remaining pair is the `a != 0 || b != 0` test, which frozen has. Call order is 100%. The real behaviour behind that test landed with this verdict: rendering into a texture removes the y-flip, so Y is recomputed as maxY * y.l, truncated with no +0.5 unlike the rounded Y above. It carries the same deliberate divergence as IStateSyncScissorRect -- the reference tests m_textureTarget's m_apiSpecific fields and frozen tests m_texture, because frozen never stores a surface in m_apiSpecific. BUILT, NOT SEEN RUNNING, and this one is visible: it changes the viewport for every render-to-texture pass, which is the shadow map and the FFX glow.

007a0d60.note: CMapEntity::FloorLight, vtable slot 3 for a unit. REWRITTEN 2026-09-27, and the 2026-09-23 note it replaces was a fair reading of the code as it then stood but is now wrong in three places, so it is worth saying what changed rather than just deleting it. That note justified a hand-set faithful status by arguing the missing calls were all frozen's decomposition: that the two operator* transforms happened in the caller, that the +0x198 loaded test had become the caller's stronger vertexCount/m_bspNodes/m_colors check, and that FUN_007aeb40 had no counterpart because frozen fused it into GroupFloorColor. None of those three is true any more. What frozen does now: this IS the virtual, with the reference's own signature (def, groupIndex, face, point), and it transforms the entity's position by the def's inverse placement ITSELF rather than receiving an already-local one. CMapObj::GroupFloorColor took the group index and took back all three of its gates, so the loaded test is where the reference has it. And FUN_007aeb40 is ported as CMapObj::GroupFaceColor, which this calls on the known-face branch -- the branch that did not exist here before and is the reason the old measurement could not see it. The probe constants are the reference's: +1.0 above the feet (DAT_009e1130) and -12.0 below (DAT_00a1047c), applied in the building's space AFTER the single transform. That ordering is what distinguishes this override from CMapDoodadDef's at 0x007c1c40, which offsets out in the world and transforms both endpoints; the two are not interchangeable for a building at any pitch or roll, and they are separate bodies in the reference for that reason. IT NO LONGER NEEDS A HAND STATUS. It measures 88% call-order recall against fresh source data and clears the 80% bar by itself, where the entry it replaces asserted faithful by hand over a measured 50%. The doodad override measures 89% and the four smaller functions in this chain measure 100%. TWO THINGS STILL DIVERGE, both real and neither hidden. The C3Vector-by-C44Matrix operator* is header-inline in frozen so it cannot appear as a call on this side at all, which costs recall without costing behaviour. And FUN_007ecef0, the DayNight block accessor, has no counterpart because frozen keeps those columns as separate CWorld statics -- see that address's own entry, which says what linking it would take. THE AMBIENT FIELD WAS AN INFERENCE AND IS NOW CONFIRMED, by a reader rather than by elimination. CMapEntity::FloorLight writes its split ambient to +0xc0 where CMapDoodadDef writes +0x84, and the question was which of frozen's fields +0xc0 is. SelectLights (FUN_007c1730), which is the SHARED slot-1 virtual on both classes, answers it: it reads the ambient as three bytes at +0x84/+0x85/+0x86 and hands them to CM2Lighting::AddAmbient, so +0x84 is the CURRENT ambient that lighting actually consumes and +0xc0 is not read there at all. That makes +0xc0 a second, separate field the current one is moved toward -- frozen's m_ambientTarget, which pairs with m_ambient exactly as its m_dirLightScaleTarget pairs with m_dirLightScale. So the two overrides differ in kind and not just in offset: a doodad is placed once and takes its floor light directly, while a unit's is written as a target and fades in. The caller-side divergence the old note ended on still stands and is still documented at FloorLightAt: frozen has no entity-to-MapObjDef-to-group parent graph, so that path brute-forces every loaded instance whose box holds the probe, and it drives the probe through the frozen-only FloorLightLocal/ApplyFloorLight pair rather than through this virtual.

006a3870.note: Its identity comes from the D3D9 device vtable offset it calls through: divide by four for the IDirect3DDevice9 method index. 0xdc / 4 = 55 = SetClipPlane, and the loop runs six times over 16-byte entries at +0x24d4 guarded by a dirty mask at +0x24d0 -- six clip planes of four floats each, which is D3D9's full complement. Device create memsets 0x60 bytes over that array, and 0x60 is 6 * sizeof(C4Plane), which confirms the count independently. This entry used to say unlinked because, as its own note put it, adding a counterpart meant adding the state and its public setter rather than just this function. That is what landed on 2026-09-23: CGxDevice now carries m_clipPlanes[6] and m_clipPlaneDirty, CGxDevice::ClipPlaneSet (FUN_00684440) stores a plane and marks it dirty only on a real change, and this walks the mask. IStateSync calls it right after IStateSyncEnables, where the reference calls it. Nothing in frozen calls ClipPlaneSet yet, so the mask stays zero and this returns on its first test. That is a correct resting state, not a stub: there is no caller whose control flow assumes it did something. GxRs_ClipPlaneMask (18) is the separate half that ENABLES planes and travels the ordinary render-state path as Ds_ClipPlaneEnable. BUILT, NOT SEEN RUNNING -- though with no caller there is nothing yet to see.

006a38d0.note: Its identity comes from the D3D9 device vtable offset it calls through: divide by four for the IDirect3DDevice9 method index. 0x12c / 4 = 75 = SetScissorRect, and the four ints it builds on the stack are a RECT clamped against the window size. Named to match the GL backend, which already had CGxDeviceGLL::IStateSyncScissorRect. Ported 2026-09-23 together with the state and setter it needed. Horizontal edges scale by DeviceCurWindow().maxX and vertical by .maxY -- the reference reaches the rect through FUN_00682d70, which is just `return &this->[0x174]`, and CRect is {minY, minX, maxY, maxX} so +0x8 is maxY and +0xc is maxX. Left and top take +0.5 (the constant at 0x009e2ec4, read out of .rdata), right and bottom +1.0. Vertical orientation flips on `+0x2918 != 0 || +0x2924 != 0`: with neither set the frame is the back buffer and top/bottom come from 1.0 - maxY and 1.0 - minY; otherwise they are used directly. IXformSetViewport flips y the same way. DIVERGENCE: those two are not the m_texture fields. Device create zeroes six consecutive dwords from +0x2910 to +0x2924, which is TextureTarget m_textureTarget[2] based at +0x2910, so +0x2918 and +0x2924 are the two m_apiSpecific fields (the reference stores one at 0x0068b929, indexing 0x2918(%edi,%eax,4) with eax = i*3). frozen tests m_texture instead, because RenderTargetSet fills m_texture and m_plane and IRenderTargetSet releases the surface without ever storing it -- testing the faithful field would make the branch permanently false and the render-to-texture case dead. Closing it properly means keeping the surface in m_apiSpecific, a lifetime change that wants a run. The dirty flag starts at 1 over an all-zero rect (device create loads 1 at 0x00688e64, the same register that initialises intF6C), so the first sync sends an empty rectangle. Harmless and faithful: D3DRS_SCISSORTESTENABLE follows GxRs_ScissorTest, which defaults to 0, so nothing clips until something enables the test and sets a rect. BUILT, NOT SEEN RUNNING.

0079d5e0.note: IDENTIFIED 2026-09-26: this is the WATER RIPPLE pass, and the records are Water0Ripple -- named by the reference itself, which uses the mangled string ".?AVWater0Ripple@@" at 0x00adfb6c as its allocation tag. Not a generic decal pass, and NOT Liquid::Draw, which the callgraph matcher had claimed: see below.  Structure. The ripples live in a TSList whose head link is the global pair at 0x00adfb5c / 0x00adfb60; the static initialiser at 0x9ce5a0 writes `(0x00adfb5c | 1)` into the second word, which is Storm's tagged-terminator convention, and is exactly what the draw's `(head & 1) == 0 && head != 0` guard tests for a non-empty list. There is also a TSGrowableArray<Water0Ripple> pool: FUN_0079d4d0 is its destructor and FUN_0079d510 its SetCount, both carrying the same tag, and both reallocating at a stride of 0x50 -- so sizeof(Water0Ripple) is 0x50. FUN_0079e2d0 tears the whole system down.  Field map, read off the walk at the top of the draw (dt is the global at 0x00cd76a0): +0x10 an angle advanced by +0x14 * dt; +0x18 the ripple's size or alpha, advanced by +0x20 * dt until it passes the limit at +0x1c -- at which point +0x20 is zeroed and the overshoot is refunded -- and by +0x24 * dt thereafter, so it is a two-phase grow-then-fade, and the ripple is unlinked once it reaches 0; +0x28 a start time gated against 0x00cd76a4; +0x2c a bucket index, 0 or 1, selecting one of two local lists the draw builds; +0x30 the TSLink the global list threads through; +0x44 the vertex or index count this ripple contributes to its bucket's total. The draw then builds a rotated quad per ripple (DecalBuildTransforms, C44Matrix::RotationAroundZ, TextureGetGxTex, BufStream, GxPrimVertexPtr, PrimIndexPtr).  WHY IT IS STILL NOT PORTED, and it is no longer the record layout: nothing would spawn a ripple. Only the static initialiser and the atexit destructor ever write the list head, so the spawn goes through the pool, and what drives it is water entry and movement over water -- and unit movement is not ported, which CLAUDE.md already records as why ribbons and footprints cannot be evaluated either. 007a2760.note: The map's segment query, the ONLY thing that fills CM2Scene::m_rayModelList -- so the ten-function ray chain finished 2026-09-27 is correct and IDLE until this lands. THE OBJECT IS CMapStaticEntity, on three independent offset matches: CMapBaseObj puts m_flags at +0x0c (the word tested for bit 0x100 and bit 0x80 of its low byte -- entity STATE flags, not the type bits, which are m_type at +0x08), and CMapStaticEntity puts m_visible at +0x25 and m_model at +0x34. IT CROSS-VALIDATES RayQuery: the linking block sets model->m_rayOwner to the ENTITY and m_rayKey to zero, so the owner a ray query returns is a CMapStaticEntity. THE PASS COUNTER at 0x00ce04c4 is incremented at 0x007a3b79 and stamped into the entity's +0x2c, so an entity straddling two chunks is linked once. Frozen models a separate traversal stamp at +0xb0; this is a second one and is not modelled. THE +0xb8/+0xbc PAIR IS NOW PART-EXPLAINED, and the conclusion REVERSES what this entry said before. The CMapDoodadDef constructor at 0x007c22xx zeroes both alongside m_model -- it is the same function that ORs Type_DoodadDef (0x40) into m_type, which confirms the class. +0xb8 is then SET from a terrain lookup: FUN_007a0530 takes the entity's m_position (+0x6c), walks CMap::GetLoadedArea then the chunk at area+0xbc, checks the hole mask and resolves a DBC record, and the caller stores its result -- or -1 when the position is not over loaded terrain. So BOTH-ZERO MEANS NEVER PLACED, not the ordinary case. Leaving the pair unmodelled does not make frozen take a merely different branch, it makes every entity look unplaced and take the branch the reference reserves for one that has not been through placement. That is why this is still not ported: the real dependency is the entity placement chain (FUN_007a0530 and its caller), which has to exist before +0xb8 means anything. The query types it writes are where the ray chain's 1/2/3 split comes from: 3 on the mask-1 path, 2 on mask-8, `(mask >> 24) & 1` on mask-0xe, and 0 on one branch of the other tree. Its two callers, FUN_007a30d0 and FUN_007a3570, are also unported, around 1150 bytes each.

007c15f0.note: ClassifyEntityInterior. Recorded 2026-09-27 as blocked on a MISSING VIRTUAL and ported the same day once that virtual existed, so the block is gone and this entry is the record of why it was ever there. What it does: fetches the group the entity was placed against (through arg2->m_mapObj, the def's root, with the group index at arg3->m_groupIndex +0x50) and marks the entity interior (m_flags +0xc bit 0x2) when that group is neither Exterior (MOGP 0x8) nor ExteriorLit (0x40), exterior (0x4) otherwise -- including when the group is absent, which is how an unloaded one reads. An interior entity then takes its floor light through vtable slot 3. THE BLOCK, and what cleared it: that slot. CMapBaseObj carried three virtuals and the reference calls a fourth here; the earlier note said adding a no-op fourth 'would let this function link while doing half of what it does, which is worse than leaving it unported', and that was right. Slot 3 is CMapStaticEntity::FloorLight, pure in the reference (the base vtable at 0x00a3fd80 holds _purecall at 0x0040baa5) and overridden by CMapEntity at 0x007a0d60 and CMapDoodadDef at 0x007c1c40. Both overrides are now ported, so the call here is the real one rather than a placeholder. One reference quirk kept deliberately: it tests the interior BIT after ORing, not the branch it just took, so an entity already interior from an earlier group is lit even when this group marks it exterior. Signature read off the disassembly at 0x007c15f0 -- a plain `ret`, so it is a free function with five stack arguments, and the face arrives by value with its ADDRESS passed on, which is what makes this the known-face path into FloorLight.

007c2a70.note: ResolveEntityGround. Ported 2026-09-27, and with it the whole chain this entry was waiting on. The entry it replaces recorded it blocked on FUN_007c28f0 and FUN_007c15f0; both are ported, as are CMap::GetTerrainType, CMapObjDef::GetPolyGroundType and everything under them. It drops a probe from 0.1 above the entity's m_collisionCenter to 1000 below and asks QueryEntityMapObj what is there. Nothing means open terrain: the entity is linked to the chunks it covers and, for a Type_Entity, m_groundType comes from CMap::GetTerrainType at m_position, with m_flags losing 0x200. A building means each collision record's group is linked through CMap::LinkToMapObjDefGroup, m_groundType comes from the WMO material under the face instead, and m_flags gains 0x200; if the surface was also interior, m_flags7c gains bit 0 and the floor light is taken through ClassifyEntityInterior on a path that RETURNS EARLY -- the only case where m_flags does not gain bit 2. m_groundType is the +0xb8 field frozen did not have. It is what the map's segment query branches on, so an entity whose placement never ran reads as standing on nothing rather than on a default surface -- which is why this chain mattered. The record slot is taken from the RENDER array (slot 0 if it holds a def, else slot 1) while the links are made from the COLLISION array. Not a misreading: the two arrays are filled by different halves of the BSP query and the reference uses each for what it knows. ONE ODDITY REPRODUCED RATHER THAN FIXED. The point handed to ClassifyEntityInterior is center.z - (end.z - start.z) * t, and because the probe points DOWN that term is negative, so the point lands ABOVE the centre instead of at the hit. The instruction at 0x007c2bcb is an fsubr and leaves no ambiguity about the sign. It reads like a slip in the original, but it shipped, so it is reproduced; revisit only behind a run that shows the floor lighting is wrong. STILL MISSING BELOW IT: FUN_007c2040, tagged as LinkEntityToChunks and left a deliberate stub. It needs FUN_006ded60 and FUN_007b5020, generic list inserts with 251 and 120 callers, which are worth identifying as their own seeding job rather than guessed at -- a wrong insert would corrupt a list every chunk walks. Nothing calls ResolveEntityGround yet, so that stub is dead code rather than a live hole.

007c28f0.note: QueryEntityMapObj. Ported 2026-09-27. The entry it replaces recorded it blocked on FUN_007c1660 and FUN_007c2700, both now ported. TWO CORRECTIONS to that earlier entry, both from reading the disassembly rather than the decompilation. First, arg5 does NOT receive a face index -- it receives the winning record's INTERIOR flag, read at +0xe of the collision array (or +0x1e for the second slot). The face lives at +0xc; the earlier note named the wrong field. Second, arg7 is the collision array and arg8 the render array, and Ghidra hides this because the function reuses arg7's STACK SLOT as a local. THE TERRAIN CHUNK IS NEVER KEPT, which is the trap here. The reference passes the address of one stack slot as CMap::GetTerrainHeight's out-chunk and then stores that function's RETURN VALUE into the same slot, so the chunk pointer is overwritten by the bool before anything reads it. Every later test on that slot is a test of whether terrain answered. Read as a chunk pointer it looks like the query keeps a chunk; it does not. What it does: asks the buildings along the segment (skipped entirely when the entity's m_flags has 0x2000), discards any record the terrain sits in FRONT of, and if neither terrain nor a building answered, rewrites the segment as a straight 1000-yard probe UP from the entity's m_collisionCenter (+0x60) and asks again. Casting up is how indoors is decided -- what matters is whether a room's geometry is overhead. m_flags7c 0x2000 drops the second record slot. The height difference is scaled by 1e-3 (DAT_009e1134) precisely because the probe is 1000 yards (DAT_009ea080), so a fraction along the segment and a height over a thousand are the same number. The no-terrain height is 100000 (DAT_00a3e6e4), far enough out that the fraction discards nothing. The two discard tests are !(fraction > distance), not fraction < distance: the x87 pair keeps the record only when the terrain is strictly further, so an equal distance or a NaN from a degenerate segment discards it. The decompilation renders this as `<`, which would keep both. ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: the reference skips the terrain query when DAT_00cf08f4 is set, the flag a global-WMO map raises when its def is created (set at 0x007bfca7, in the function that builds a CMapObjDef's radius and m_mapObj). frozen tracks no such flag. Leaving the query in is equivalent where it matters -- a map with no ADT grid has no loaded area, so GetTerrainHeight answers false by itself -- but not provably so for a map carrying both, hence recorded here.

007c2700.note: QueryMapObjDefSegment. Ported 2026-09-27, 486 bytes, and with it the whole placed-building segment query is ported: this, QueryDefSegment (007c25d0), QueryDefGroupSegment (007c1dc0) and CMapObj::SegmentVsPortals (007af520). Two ways in. arg6 is a CMapChunk -- its m_mapObjDefLinkList is the list the reference reads at +0xd8 with the stride at +0xd0, which frozen already had at +0xd0 -- and with one given, only that chunk's buildings are asked. With null, every placed building in CMapObjDef::s_uniqueIds is (the global hash at DAT_00d25438/DAT_00d25440). Both skip a def with m_flags 0x20 and reject the rest on the MODF box first. BOTH RECORD ARRAYS HOLD TWO ENTRIES and the tail is entirely about reconciling the four. They start empty at distance 1.05 (DAT_00a40314, past the segment's end so any real hit beats them), then: a collision slot that found nothing takes the render slot's hit; if slot 0 is still empty, slot 1 slides into it in BOTH arrays and slot 1 is emptied, and if slot 1 was empty too the function returns false; finally a render slot that found nothing takes the collision hit with its face forced to 0xffff. That last 0xffff is deliberate and should not be tidied away: the record is standing in for a render hit that never happened, and the face says so rather than naming a polygon that was never tested. The whole tail was read off the disassembly at 0x007c2815 through 0x007c28e5, because Ghidra renders it as goto soup across two loop bodies.

007c25d0.note: QueryDefSegment. Ported 2026-09-27, and the entry it replaces recorded it blocked on FUN_007c1dc0, which is now ported as QueryDefGroupSegment. One placed building's answer to a segment, over all its groups. All three query points are brought into the building's space through the def's inverse placement (+0xb0) once and nothing is transformed back, because the hit records carry a distance rather than a position. It walks m_defGroupLinkList (+0x11c, stride at +0x114) and gates each group on three tests: none of 0x410080 set (exterior, skybox and the rest -- the same mask QuerySegmentMapObjs already uses), the segment reaching the group's bounds, and a point test that only sometimes applies -- an exterior group with the def's 0x400 clear is taken on bounds alone, everything else has to contain the third point via CMapObj::PointInGroupBox. WATCH THE SLOT POLARITY. The two record arrays hold two entries each and this picks by the def's m_flags 0x400: bit SET writes entry 0, bit CLEAR writes entry 1. Its sibling walk QuerySegmentMapObjs (FUN_007d59b0) uses the OPPOSITE convention for the same flag, and frozen's port of that one is right for it -- both were read off their own disassembly at 0x007c26aa and 0x007d5a1c rather than inferred from each other. Do not make them agree. These two are parallel implementations in the reference, not one calling the other: 007d59b0 lives in MapChunkLiquid.cpp and uses CMapObjGroup::QuerySegment with CMapObj::QuerySegmentPortals, while this chain lives in MapMem.cpp and uses QuerySegmentDual with CMapObj::SegmentVsPortals. Checked before porting, so this is not a duplicate of the walk already inside QuerySegmentMapObjs.

007c1dc0.note: QueryDefGroupSegment. Ported 2026-09-27, 345 bytes. The entry that stood here recorded it as blocked on FUN_007af520 and FUN_007917b0; the first is ported and the second is resolved as a divergence, so nothing blocks it. It asks one placed building group both halves of a segment query at once. CMapObjGroup::QuerySegmentDual, which frozen already had with exactly this shape, returns a collision hit and a render hit -- different surfaces, since a doorway's collision volume is not its drawn geometry -- and a face of -1 from either half leaves that half's record ALONE rather than clearing it, because the caller accumulates across groups. The portal pass runs only for an interior group (MOGP bit 3 clear) and only replaces the collision record: if the nearest portal crossing beats the geometry hit, the record's group becomes the one on the far side and the face becomes 0xffff. That 0xffff means 'left through a doorway', not 'nothing found'. An earlier note here called this a liquid pass; it is portals. Two numbers read out of .rdata rather than guessed: the portal search starts at 1.05 of the segment (DAT_00a40314, deliberately past the far end so a portal on the endpoint is still found) and has to beat the geometry by 1e-4 (DAT_009e8cd0). The reference's x87 pair for that second test has its `jp` taken unless the difference is strictly less, so an equal or NaN difference does not replace the record -- which a plain C `<` reproduces. SMapObjHit carries no size assert on purpose: the reference packs the record into 16 bytes with 32-bit pointers and frozen is a 64-bit build, so it measures 24. Nothing reads it from a file or steps it by a baked stride.

007af520.note: CMapObj::SegmentVsPortals. Ported 2026-09-27, 542 bytes. CORRECTION: the entry written earlier the same day called this 'a segment against one group's liquid surface'. That was wrong and this is a PORTAL query. The three arrays it walks are the WMO portal chunks, and frozen already had all of them at the offsets the disassembly uses -- m_mopv at +0x134 (portal vertices, C3Vector), m_mopt at +0x138 (SMOPortal, stride 0x14, the C4Plane at +4) and m_mopr at +0x13c (SMOPortalRef, stride 8) -- with the group's own MOPR range at m_portalStart +0x50 and m_portalCount +0x54. PointInPolygon against MOPV is what settles it: liquid has no polygon to be inside. What it does: walks the group's MOPR range, intersects the normalised ray with each portal's plane (epsilon 0.1, DAT_009e3004), keeps the crossing only when the hit lands inside the portal polygon, and narrows to the nearest. `t` is a FRACTION of the segment in and out while the walk runs in ray units, which is why the length is multiplied in and divided out. The output order is two signs agreeing: the plane evaluated at the segment's START, and MOPR's own `side`. Ghidra renders the first as `0.0 < f == (f == 0.0)`, which by the x87 rule is `f < 0`; with its NaN term the condition is exactly !(f >= 0), so a NaN distance counts as behind. Its three callees were already frozen's: DominantAxis, IntersectRayPlane, PointInPolygon.

007917b0.note: The element accessor for the reference's def-group array, and frozen has no counterpart BY DESIGN. Resolved 2026-09-27 from its one call site, which settles what an earlier note could not read off the body: the ecx is `def + 0x120`, so the container is CMapObjDef's def-group array. The reference keeps the first four groups INLINE in the def and spills to the heap past that, which is exactly what the body tests -- a sentinel at +0x10 of the container (def +0x130) reading -1 means spilled, so the data is at the pointer in +0x8 (def +0x128); otherwise the data starts at the container itself. The accessor exists only to hide that choice. frozen replaced the whole scheme with TSGrowableArray<CMapObjDefGroup*> m_defGroups, a divergence CMapObjDef.hpp already documented at those offsets before this function was looked at. CORRECTION to this entry's own first draft: it claimed the counterpart was a header-only template subscript that could never appear in frozen's inventory, and the callgraph matcher promptly bound it to TSBaseArray<CMapObjDefGroup *>::operator[], which the PDB does carry. So the link exists and is automatic; what diverges is only the STORAGE, four inline slots plus a heap spill against a growable array. Kept diverged rather than unlinked for that reason -- there is nothing left to port, and unlike unlinked, diverged does not veto the automatic match.

0072a000.note: CGUnit_C::GetUnitName -- NOT CGObject::GetType, which is what the callgraph matcher had claimed and what this entry exists to refuse. Analysed 2026-09-27, not ported. THE FALSE LINK, and why it could not be right: frozen's CGObject::GetType is a one-line accessor returning an OBJECT_TYPE enum. This function is 651 bytes, returns a char*, references the string "UNKNOWNOBJECT", and calls FrameScript_GetText, WowClientDB<SpellRec>::GetRecord and ClntObjMgrObjectPtr. An enum getter does none of that. The link held its recall at 0% with an EMPTY frozen side -- twelve reference calls against none -- which is the clearest tell there is. WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS: the display name of a unit, with two twists. Its second argument is an out-parameter that receives the unit's TITLE (the subname at +0x34 of the creature record) when the caller passes one; its third says whether to honour a TRANSFORM. With that set and the unit carrying the +0xf42 bit 0x80, it walks the aura list (entries at +0xc50, count +0xc54, with the overflow array at +0xc58 selected when +0xdd0 is not -1), looks each aura's SpellRec up and watches for effect 0x117; on a hit it returns the impersonated unit's name instead, recursing into itself with the transform flag cleared. Otherwise it goes to the name cache and falls back to the localized UNKNOWNOBJECT string, then to the literal "Unknown Being". frozen ALREADY NAMES IT: CGUnit_C::RefreshDataPointers carries `// TODO auto name = this->GetUnitName(0, 1);` beside a SysMsgPrintf for a missing display id -- the same two arguments in the same order. WHAT IT NEEDS: nine unidentified helpers -- FUN_004f8850 and FUN_005eeb70 (the aura-list lock pair), FUN_008b7da0, FUN_0067d770 and FUN_0067ea30 (name-cache lookups, where frozen already has NameCache.cpp and NameCacheGetName), FUN_0074d750, FUN_0074f400, FUN_0067a940 and the callback FUN_00728ca0. The name-cache pair is the place to start, because frozen has the module for it.

00825750.note: CM2Model::GetWorldBounds. Ported 2026-09-27 from the analysis recorded here the cycle before. Which box it starts from depends on whether the model has PARTICLES: with them it takes the model's global box, which is already conservative enough to hold them; without, the tighter box authored on the current sequence, with the ribbons unioned in. The placement is matrixB4, or matrixF4 taken back out of the scene's view (m_scene->m_viewInv) when the model hangs off a parent. TWO QUIRKS REPRODUCED. An authored box that is INVERTED is left untransformed and still used -- TransformBox on one would produce something worse than the sentinel it already is. And the particle loop is dead twice over: it only runs when the model has no particles (the branch at 0x0082577b jumps into this path on a zero count), and it grows a box that was already copied out a few lines earlier, so even if it ran the result would be discarded. 00834660.note: CM2Model::CollectShadowCasters. Ported 2026-09-27. Walks a model's batches, keeps the ones solid enough to cast a shadow, files each into one of two lists by its shader field, then recurses into everything attached. WHY IT MATTERS, which took three cycles to establish: frozen's shadow pass currently reuses the scene's OPAQUE draw list, which requires alpha >= 0.99999, while this gate is 0.55. A batch between the two casts a shadow in the reference and nothing in frozen -- the whole band of partial transparency. The two thresholds answer different questions and the reference builds this collector precisely because the draw pass is the wrong set. Written up under the 2026-09-27 heading in docs/ref/parity-shadows.md. The gate is alpha19C times m_colors[colorIndex].alphaTrack.currentValue (when colorIndex is in range) times m_textureWeights[textureWeightCombos[batch.textureWeightComboIndex]].weightTrack.currentValue (when textureCount is non-zero), against 0.55 (DAT_009edce0). A batch is skipped unless its shader is not -0x8000 read SIGNED, flags bit 2 is clear and materialLayer is zero; its material must lack 0x40 and either carry 0x80 or have a blend mode of 0 or 1. Offsets confirmed rather than assumed: M2Batch is 0x18 and every field lined up, M2SkinProfile::batches sits at +0x24/+0x28 exactly as the reference reads it, and CM2Model +0x9c is m_skinSections (indexed by skinSectionIndex), +0xa0 m_colors, +0xa8 m_textureWeights -- the chain checked by matrixB4 landing on +0xb4. ONE BRANCH NOT WRITTEN: the reference takes its batches from ptr2D0 when that is set and skips the skin-section test. frozen never builds ptr2D0 and M2OptimizedGeometry has no definition, so it cannot be dereferenced here; every other path in the file takes the same unoptimized branch for the same reason. NOT YET WIRED: CM2Scene::DrawShadowCasters still submits the opaque pass. Making this the caster source is the change that actually fixes the shadows, and it wants a run.

00823d50.note: M2ShadowCasterList::Add. Ported 2026-09-27 together with its caller. Appends {model, batchIndex, 1} at data + count * 0xc and bumps the count, or DROPS the caster silently when the array is full -- that drop is the reference's own behaviour and is kept visible rather than turned into an assert. The container is a plain {data, count, capacity} triple. The reference keeps TWO of them adjacent in one 24-byte block and picks between them by the batch's shader field, which is why its callers pass p and p + 0xc. frozen's record measures 16 bytes rather than 12 because its pointer is 64-bit; nothing reads it from a file or steps it by a baked stride, so no size assert.

00831990.note: CM2Model::AnimateAlphasOnly. Ported 2026-09-27 off the spec recorded here the cycle before; the three items that spec listed as unread are all closed. It is AnimateMTSimple with everything but the alphas removed -- the colour records' alpha tracks and the texture weight tracks, both defaulting to 1.0 through M2AnimateTrack<fixed16, float>. That is exactly what its one caller needs: the batch collection walk multiplies model alpha by texture weight by colour alpha and tests the product against 0.55, and animating anything else would be wasted. THE THREE OPEN ITEMS, settled: FUN_00407f80 is C44Matrix::operator= -- a sixteen-dword copy with 247 callers -- so the line reads matrixF4 = matrixB4 * m_scene->m_view, the same assignment and operand order AnimateMTSimple already makes. Reproduced -- the loops are idempotent within a frame, so that costs work rather than a wrong answer. The third was m_shared +0x198, a uint16 the reference's constructor zeroes along with the run from +0x16c to +0x1a4. What sets it is still unidentified; the only 16-bit write to that offset anywhere in the binary is that clear. frozen now carries it as CM2Shared::uint198, never written, so the fall-back condition keeps both of its terms instead of being written with half. The colour loop animates the ALPHA track and not the colour one: the reference reads M2Color +0x14 and writes M2ModelColor +0x14, and M2Track is 0x14 bytes, so +0x14 is alphaTrack in both.
